newsitem.title: UK: Heavy N Sea maintenance programme seen in August.
newsitem.headline: Heavy N Sea maintenance programme seen in August.

text.p: Oilfield maintenance in both the Norwegian and British North Sea sectors will eat deep into crude output in August, a Reuters survey of field operators showed.

Some 7.6 million barrels, an average of 245,000 barrels per day, will be lost to the work against July production. That sum equates to a shortfall of around 15 standard 500,000 barrel cargoes from the August loading programme.

Daily liftings in July were scheduled at 4.49 million bpd, up from 4.30 million bpd in June, when a heavy maintenance programme cost operators between 350,000 and 400,000 bpd in lost output, or between 21 and 27 cargoes.

The effect of maintenance on Norwegian production will be less than the 10 percent decline anticipated earlier in the year, but is made up for by recently announced upgrade work on part of the Brent system.

The BP operated Magnus field, which feeds through the Ninian pipeline to Sullom Voe, is to shut for the last two weeks of August, cutting 109,000 barrels per day from the Brent blend loading programme.
The Brent Bravo field, with an average production of 70,000 bpd, will shut for one week in August.
Norwegian state oil company Statoil plans a two-week stoppage at its Statfjord B platform from August 9, which will reduce Statfjord loadings by 2.1 million bpd.
Other planned Norwegian turnarounds have been truncated, but still remain substantial, at some 5.24 million barrels.
Work at Gullfaks A and B will last from August 28 to September 15, rather than for 25 days as first planned. Their average output is 265,000 bpd.
The 113,000 bpd Sleipner East gas and condensate field is still tentatively scheduled to shut down for 12 days from August 7.
Norsk Hydro has cut its planned work at the 210,000 bpd Troll West field from 14 days to five days, officials said.
Operator Shell Expro's offshore Kittiwake field, with an average output of 22,000 bpd, will be shut down from July 28 to August 13.
But in the British sector an August turnaround at the 10,000 bpd Auk field in the Fulmar system has been cancelled by operator Shell. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
